metadata.title: Jeremy McNichols likely out for season
metadata.description: Commanders head coach Dan Quinn said Jeremy McNichols will likely be out for the season.
metadata.analysis: McNichols was placed on injured reserve on Tuesday.

metadata.title: Jeremy McNichols - Done for season with foot injury
metadata.description: McNichols, who suffered a foot injury Sunday against the Eagles that may require surgery, is out for the season, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
metadata.analysis: McNichols was placed on injured reserve Tuesday, and what coach Dan Quinn described as a "serious mid-foot injury" will keep the running back sidelined for the rest of the 2026 campaign. With Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) slated to miss at least two more games, the Commanders' current healthy RBs are Rachaad White, Austin Ekeler and Robert Henry.

metadata.title: Jeremy McNichols - Heads to injured reserve
metadata.description: The Commanders placed McNichols (foot) on injured reserve Tuesday.
metadata.analysis: McNichols' move to IR ensures that he'll miss at least the Commanders' next four games, but Tashan Reed of The Washington Post relays that the running back isn't expected to play again this season after sustaining what head coach Dan Quinn labeled as a "serious mid-foot injury" during Sunday's win over the Eagles. The 30-year-old is still seeking further medical opinions, so a formal timeline for McNichols' recovery hasn't yet been established. In response to McNichols' injury, Washington claimed Robert Henry off waivers from Seattle on Tuesday to bolster their depth at running back behind Rachaad White and Austin Ekeler.

metadata.title: Jeremy McNichols placed on IR
metadata.description: The Commanders placed RB Jeremy McNichols on injured reserve.
metadata.analysis: McNichols suffered the injury in Sunday's win over the Eagles. He will miss at least the next four weeks.

metadata.title: Jeremy McNichols Goes on IR, Not Expected Back This Season
metadata.description: The Washington Commanders placed running back Jeremy McNichols (foot) on Injured Reserve on Tuesday, and he is not expected to return this season, according to Tashan Reed of The Washington Post. It is the second time this year that McNichols has been on IR, and it will also be the last. The 30-year-old veteran injured his foot in the third quarter of the Sunday night win over the division-rival Philadelphia Eagles and never returned. He will finish his ninth year in the NFL (third with the Commanders) with only 10 carries for 34 yards and one reception for a seven-yard gain in just two games played. The Commanders also have second-year back Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) on Injured Reserve, so they are now down to Rachaad White and Austin Ekeler as their primary RBs as they head into a Week 9 contest at home against the Los Angeles Rams. With Croskey-Merritt out for at least three more games, one of Craig Reynolds or Devin Neal will likely be promoted to the active roster for this weekend's game.

metadata.title: Jeremy McNichols - May miss months
metadata.description: McNichols is getting additional opinions on the foot injury that he suffered Sunday against the Eagles, but there's an expectation that he'll miss multiple months, Tashan Reed of The Washington Post reports.
metadata.analysis: McNichols limped to the locker room in the third quarter of Sunday's game in the third quarter and didn't return. Head coach Dan Quinn told Nicki Jhabvala of The Athletic on Monday that McNichols has a "mid-foot" injury that may be "serious," and Reed's new report backs up that sentiment. With Jacory Croskey-Merritt out at least three more games while on IR due to a groin issue, Rachaad White and Austin Ekeler are the healthy running backs on the Commanders' active roster.

metadata.title: Jeremy McNichols - Mid-foot injury is concerning
metadata.description: Coach Dan Quinn said Monday that McNichols has a "mid-foot" injury, while adding that the team is concerned that it's a serious issue for the running back, Nicki Jhabvala of The Athletic reports.
metadata.analysis: With Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) on IR and in line to miss at least two more games, the Commanders may need add RB depth behind Rachaad White and Austin Ekeler in the coming days. In addition to the possibility of adding a free agent backfield option, the team also has Devin Neal and Craig Reynolds on the practice squad.

metadata.title: Jeremy McNichols Expected to Miss Multiple Months With Foot Injury
metadata.description: While Washington Commanders running back Jeremy McNichols (foot) is getting additional opinions on his foot injury on Tuesday, he is expected to miss multiple months, a source told Tashan Reed of The Washington Post. Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) is already on Injured Reserve, so Washington's healthy RBs are now Rachaad White, Austin Ekeler, Craig Reynolds, and Devin Neal. The 30-year-old McNichols injured his foot in the third quarter of the Sunday night win over the division-rival Philadelphia Eagles in Week 8 and never returned, and now it looks like he could miss the rest of the 2026 regular season. Croskey-Merritt will miss at least three more games, which makes White the Commanders' clear RB1 going forward, although he should continue to split backfield work with Ekeler. McNichols was not on the fantasy radar, outside of deep leagues, even with JCM injured. He had 10 carries for 34 yards in his two games played this year and failed to go over 261 yards rushing in either of his first two seasons with the Commanders. McNichols' injury makes Ekeler more attractive as a deep-league waiver-wire pickup going into a Week 9 tilt against the Los Angeles Rams.

metadata.title: Jeremy McNichols' Injury Could Prompt Commanders to Add Running Back
metadata.description: Washington Commanders running back Jeremy McNichols (foot) is undergoing further evaluation after suffering a midfoot injury during Sunday's 27-10 victory over the Philadelphia Eagles. Head coach Dan Quinn indicated Monday that Washington could explore signing a free agent or promoting someone from its practice squad, according to JP Finlay of NBC Sports Washington. McNichols exited in the third quarter after rushing for 21 yards on five carries and catching one pass for seven yards. His injury leaves Washington thin in the backfield, with Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) already on injured reserve. Rachaad White and Austin Ekeler are the team's remaining healthy running backs on the active roster, while Devin Neal and Craig Reynolds are available on the practice squad. White led Washington with 55 rushing yards and a touchdown against Philadelphia, while Ekeler contributed 36 yards on eight carries. White carries the stronger immediate fantasy appeal if McNichols misses time, although Washington's potential roster addition could affect the backfield rotation.

metadata.title: Commanders Concerned Jeremy McNichols' Foot Injury is "Serious"
metadata.description: Washington Commanders head coach Dan Quinn said on Monday that running back Jeremy McNichols (foot) has a "mid-foot" injury, and the team is "concerned it's serious," according to Nicki Jhabvala of The Athletic. McNichols suffered the foot injury in the second half of the Sunday night win over the division-rival Philadelphia Eagles and did not return. With Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) on Injured Reserve, Washington's backfield depth is thinning out, with Rachaad White and veteran Austin Ekeler now the top two backs as the team heads into a Week 9 matchup at home against the Los Angeles Rams. The 30-year-old McNichols will almost certainly not be available this weekend, and he could join Croskey-Merritt on IR. The Commanders have Devin Neal and Craig Reynolds on their practice squad, and one of those RBs is expected to be elevated to the active roster for Week 9. McNichols has only appeared in two games this year due to injury and has 10 carries for 34 yards (3.4 yards per attempt) while catching his only target for seven yards.

metadata.title: Jeremy McNichols runs for 21 yards, leaves with foot injury on SNF
metadata.description: Jeremy McNichols carried the ball five times for 21 yards and caught his lone target for seven yards in a 27-10 win over the Eagles in Week 8.
metadata.analysis: McNichols looked solid operating as a change-of-pace back but he injured his foot in the third quarter and did not return to the game. His status is up in the air heading into a Week 9 matchup against the Rams.

metadata.title: Jeremy McNichols - Questionable to return due to foot
metadata.description: McNichols (foot) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Eagles.
metadata.analysis: The Commanders clarified the nature of McNichols' injury shortly after he headed to the locker room while exhibiting a limp in the third quarter. Prior to getting hurt, McNichols had five carries for 21 yards and caught his only target for seven yards while working in a rotational role alongside Rachaad White and Austin Ekeler in the absence of Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin).

metadata.title: Jeremy McNichols - Injured against Eagles
metadata.description: McNichols headed back to the locker room in the second half of Sunday's game against the Eagles and was walking with a limp, Tashan Reed of The Washington Post reports.
metadata.analysis: McNichols was checked for an injury in the blue tent before heading to the locker room. While the exact nature of his injury has yet to be clarified, the running back can be considered questionable to return after rushing five times for 21 yards and catching his lone target for seven yards prior to exiting. Rachaad White and Austin Ekeler are the two remaining healthy options in Washington's backfield rotation.

metadata.title: Jeremy McNichols Questionable to Return with Foot Injury
metadata.description: Washington Commanders running back Jeremy McNichols (foot) is considered questionable to return during Sunday's game against the Philadelphia Eagles. McNichols was forced to exit during the second half of this game due to a foot issue, and it's unclear if he'll be able to finish out this game. Before leaving, McNichols carried the ball five times for 21 yards and also hauled in one pass for seven additional yards through the air. If he's unable to return, Rachaad White and Austin Ekeler will see a slight uptick in workload over the final quarter of this game.

metadata.title: Jeremy McNichols A Deep-League Option After Return From IR
metadata.description: Washington Commanders running back Jeremy McNichols was activated from IR before the team's Week 6 loss to the 49ers and could be in the mix at the position as the Commanders return from a Week 7 bye. McNichols landed on IR with a lingering quad injury he suffered in mid-August, and he played 12 snaps (18%) in his return, taking five carries for 13 yards in San Francisco. With Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) placed on IR and not eligible to return until Week 11 at the earliest, McNichols will likely mix in with veterans Rachaad White and Austin Ekeler for the next few weeks. McNichols could be the favorite for short-yardage and early down work, which gives him touchdown-dependent potential if the Washington offense gets going. The Commanders host the Eagles on Sunday Night Football of Week 8 in a favorable matchup, so McNichols is worth a look if you are in a deep league and need running back help.

metadata.title: Jeremy McNichols - Minimally involved Monday night
metadata.description: McNichols accrued five rushes for 13 yards during Monday's 23-17 loss to the 49ers.
metadata.analysis: With Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) sidelined, the Commanders turned to Rachaad White to do most of the heavy lifting at the running back position. McNichols, who was activated from injured reserve ahead of the Week 6 meeting with the 49ers after missing the first five games of the 2026 campaign, logged 12 offensive snaps, five more than Austin Ekeler (seven). However, neither McNichols nor Ekeler got anything going, with both players combining for six carries. With Croskey-Merritt now on injured reserve, there is room for others to step up, though it's likely White will remain the workhorse, with Ekeler and McNichols getting the leftover scraps.

metadata.title: Jeremy McNichols - Activated from IR
metadata.description: McNichols (quadriceps) was activated from injured reserve by the Commanders on Monday.
metadata.analysis: McNichols is officially active for Monday night's matchup with San Francisco, returning to action after missing the team's first five games of the regular season while recovering from a quad injury. The running back logged three consecutive full practices to end the week, so he should be back to full health. With Jacory Croskey-Merritt (foot) sidelined in Week 6, McNichols will have a chance to carve out a significant role in the backfield while splitting touches with Rachaad White and Austin Ekeler versus the 49ers.

metadata.title: Jeremy McNichols (quad) activated from IR
metadata.description: The Commanders activated Jeremy McNichols from injured reserve.
metadata.analysis: McNichols will be good to go for Monday's game against the 49ers. He'll add depth in the Commanders backfield.

metadata.title: Jeremy McNichols - Deemed questionable for MNF
metadata.description: McNichols (quadriceps) is questionable for Monday night's game against the 49ers.

With Jacory Croskey-Merritt (foot) out, the Commanders could use McNichols as depth alongside Rachaad White and Austin Ekeler.

metadata.title: Jeremy McNichols - Another full practice
metadata.description: McNichols (quadriceps) was a full participant in Friday's practice.
metadata.analysis: McNichols has opened Week 6 prep with back-to-back full practices, which indicates that the veteran running back is in the final stages of his recovery from a quad injury that caused him to open the regular season on injured reserve. He would need to be activated from IR in order to be eligible to play against the 49ers on Monday. McNichols' return could be a crucial one for the Commanders, whose backfield is dealing with injuries to Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin), Rachaad White (shoulder) and Austin Ekeler (chest).

metadata.title: Jeremy McNichols (quad) to practice fully this week

metadata.analysis: McNichols is continuing to work his way back from a quad injury. He remains off the fantasy radar.

metadata.title: Jeremy McNichols - Ruled out for Week 5
metadata.description: McNichols (quadriceps) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Giants.
metadata.analysis: McNichols remains on injured reserve, so his next chance to suit up will be in Week 6 against the 49ers on Monday night. The Commanders will continue to roll with Jacory Croskey-Merritt, Rachaad White, Austin Ekeler and special-teamer Craig Reynolds out of the backfield.

metadata.title: Jeremy McNichols - Questionable for Sunday
metadata.description: McNichols (quadriceps) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Giants.
metadata.analysis: The Commanders opened McNichols' 21-day practice window to return from IR on Wednesday. The running back logged limited practices throughout Week 5 prep and remains questionable for Sunday's game. The team still has over two weeks to ramp up the 30-year-old's practice participation before it must make a decision about his status for the remainder of the 2026 season.

metadata.title: Jeremy McNichols - Logs another limited practice Thursday
metadata.description: McNichols (quadriceps) was a limited participant at practice Thursday.
metadata.analysis: The Commanders opened McNichols' 21-day practice window to be activated from IR Wednesday, but it's still up in the air whether that activation will happen ahead of Sunday's game versus the Giants. He'll likely at least have to manage a full practice before returning to game action, and Friday will be his last chance to do that for Week 5.

metadata.title: Jeremy McNichols (quad) limited participant Thursday
metadata.description: Jeremy McNichols (quad) was a limited participant at practice on Thursday.
metadata.analysis: McNichols was again limited at practice on Thursday. He's still in his 21-day practice window and has yet to be officially activated, so it remains to be seen whether or not he will be a part of Washington's backfield rotation in Week 5.
